reader_input:
--- SLIDE 1 of 10 ---
Headline: Claude Code now makes videos.
Text:
- CHASE AI
- (for free)
- No video editor. No AI video credits. Runs on your Claude plan.
- made by Claude Code, Claude's coding app · one prompt
[A still from a finished video Claude Code made from one short prompt: the word CLAUDE in white letters orbiting an orange ring on black, inside a video player with a play button]

--- SLIDE 2 of 10 ---
Headline: Not AI video. Code that draws.
Text:
- WHAT IT IS
- AI video tools guess every pixel. Claude Code writes code that draws each picture, then joins the pictures into an MP4 video.
- drawn by hand
- AI video
- You describe it → Claude codes every picture → checks them → you get an MP4
[A frame from a video Claude Code made: a circle-and-wave animation, with the words 'drawn by hand' and 'AI video' crossed out underneath]

--- SLIDE 3 of 10 ---
Headline: The only bill: your Claude plan
Text:
- WHAT IT COSTS
- Video editing software | $0 · not needed
- AI video generator credits | $0 · not needed
- The 2 tools it runs on your computer | $0 · free and open source
- Voice-over | optional
- Your Claude plan | the one you already have
- Total extra: $0
- Free ≠ unlimited: videos count toward your Claude usage limits.
[A receipt: video software $0, AI video credits $0, the 2 tools $0, voice-over optional, your Claude plan, total extra $0]

--- SLIDE 4 of 10 ---
Headline: A video is 60 pictures a second
Text:
- HOW IT WORKS
- 1 · JavaScript: the code language web pages run on
- 2 · Playwright: a hidden copy of Chrome that draws each frame
- 3 · Frame: one picture. 60 make one second.
- 4 · FFmpeg: a free tool that stitches frames into an MP4
- Playwright and FFmpeg are both free and open source.
[Diagram from the explainer Claude made about itself: a box of code, a browser drawing a circle-and-wave picture, a stack of frames, FFmpeg, a video play button; numbered 1-4 to match the labels]

--- SLIDE 5 of 10 ---
Headline: It checks its own work
Text:
- THE LOOP
- This is the part that makes it click.
- Claude can't watch a video. So it pulls a contact sheet: one image with many frames in a grid. It spots what's wrong, fixes the code, re-renders and repeats.
- Before: label cut off
- After: fixed
- Shown in the explainer Claude made about itself.
[Two contact sheets side by side from Claude's own explainer: before, frames flagged where a label is cut off; after, the same frames with checkmarks]

--- SLIDE 6 of 10 ---
Headline: Ask for a storyboard first
Text:
- PRO TIP
- A full render can take 20+ minutes. So ask for a storyboard first: one page with a key frame for every scene. Approve it before the long build starts.
- Storyboard: one key frame per scene
- 7 scenes to approve before the full build
[A real storyboard page: 7 numbered key frames of the planned video, each with its timing and sound, and a note to give each panel a thumbs up or down]

--- SLIDE 7 of 10 ---
Headline: Paste this into Claude Code
Text:
- THE PROMPT
- PROMPT
- Make a 30-second animated explainer of how [TOPIC] works, 16:9.
- Build it in JavaScript on a canvas, with a soundtrack generated in code,
- and render it to an MP4 with Playwright and FFmpeg.
- Before you call it done, use FFmpeg to pull a contact sheet,
- look at it, fix what's wrong, re-render, and repeat.
- + add: “Storyboard it first and wait for my OK.”
- [TOPIC] = your subject · canvas = a drawing area on a web page · 16:9 = widescreen
- First time? Step 2 on slide 9 installs the free tools for you.
[The prompt as a clean text card with one key line under it]

--- SLIDE 8 of 10 ---
Headline: Three real videos it made
Text:
- PROOF
- 1 · An explainer of how it all works, made in one attempt
- 2 · A 15-second motion-graphics reel from one short prompt
- 3 · A history video in a reference video's style, new subject
- Reference video
- Claude Code's remake
[Three real frames: a dark circle-and-wave explainer, a frame from the motion reel, and a side-by-side of an old-paper history video and Claude's remake in the same style]

--- SLIDE 9 of 10 ---
Headline: Start here: 3 steps
Text:
- START HERE
- 1 · Comment ANIMATE. I'll send you my free animate skill: a saved set of steps Claude Code follows.
- 2 · Paste its link into Claude Code. It installs the free tools for you.
- 3 · Type:
- /animate a 45-second history of the bicycle, cut paper
- Styles: cut paper, crosshatch, riso, sketchbook, math, pixel, isometric, or your own look
[A command card with the /animate line above a strip of 7 small sample frames, one per style]

--- SLIDE 10 of 10 ---
Headline: Comment ANIMATE
Text:
- GET THE SKILL
- I'll send you my free animate skill + the install steps.
[Text-only CTA: big Comment ANIMATE in a hand-drawn speech bubble, no evidence]
